dct_description_sm: As part of the ArcticKelp project, funded by ArcticNet and supported by Polar Knowledge Canada, researchers from Universit Laval and the Canadian Museum of Nature conducted surveys of shallow coastal habitats (<25 m) and environmental conditions in the central Kitikmeot region of the Canadian Arctic. The objectives were to: (1) characterize the regional seascape by mapping substrate type and kelp cover; (2) identify the environmental drivers influencing kelp forest distribution; and (3) evaluate macrofaunal richness and community composition across the main habitat types (bare, kelp-adjacent, and kelp forest). Fieldwork was conducted from small vessels along shallow coastal areas of Iqaluktuuttiaq (Cambridge Bay) Dease Strait and Queen Maud Gulf within a ~60 km radius of Iqaluktuuttiaq, over three consecutive field seasons (20222024), between mid-August and mid-September.
dct_title_s: Coastal Environmental Dataset for the Central Kitikmeot, ArcticKelp (2023, 2024)
